facts.fact: The Nation reports a National Local Government Finance Committee presentation to a meeting with the Ministry of Local Government and councils in Mzuzu in the week before 22 September 2022 (the article's published date; the page is undated) as stating a lack of local authority IFMIS connectivity: the real-time network the government intended never happened, the council's local network links only the District Commissioner's or chief executive's office to the council's own data centre, most servers in many councils do not work properly and data is consolidated by hand.

The Nation reports the Malawi Local Government Association's executive director saying in September 2022 (the article's published date; the page is undated) that councils use the new central government IFMIS to process salary payments and nothing else yet, and that efforts to link the local IFMIS with the central one have produced nothing on the ground; the article does not say from where or over what connection councils reach the central system.
facts.system: Central government IFMIS, used by councils for salaries

systems.platform: Serenic Navigator, unsupported by Microsoft since 2020 and not upgraded since 2014; supplier TechnoBrain's contract terminated
systems.owner: National Local Government Finance Committee, the main ICT hub for local authorities
systems.tiers: councils, each on its own servers at council headquarters; not linked to the central government IFMIS
central government; councils use it for salary payments only

systems.system: Council local area network and servers
systems.country_label: local area network [LAN] in the councils
systems.tiers: connects only the District Commissioner's or chief executive officer's office to the council's data centre; servers old and failing in many councils

note: The two facts pull apart and the parent must weigh them: the finance committee says the councils' own finance system has no network to the centre, while the association says councils do process salaries in the central system. The `none` is the document's statement about the finance system's connectivity, not a statement that council offices have no internet at all.
